name: Learn: Autoscaling (HPA)
objective: CKAD › Application Deployment. Create HorizontalPodAutoscalers: imperative autoscale, autoscaling/v2 with memory and multiple metrics, scaling behavior, and the no-requests diagnose-fix. Graded on the HPA object (this bench has no metrics-server, so actual scaling needs one).
description: Five strict HPA practicals against pre-seeded Deployments. Each Check shows which requirements you met and why any failed.

questions.title: Autoscale a Deployment (imperative)
questions.teach:
An **HPA** scales a Deployment's replicas on observed metrics. Create one fast: `kubectl autoscale deployment <d> --name <h> --cpu-percent=70 --min=2 --max=10`.

**Gotcha:** the target Deployment must set resource **requests** for that metric, or the HPA can't compute utilization (shows `<unknown>`).
questions.prompt:
In `hpa-learn`, create an HPA named `web-hpa` for Deployment `web`: target **70%** average CPU, min **2**, max **10**.

Target: `web-hpa` → scaleTargetRef `web`, minReplicas 2, maxReplicas 10, CPU Utilization 70%.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n hpa-learn autoscale deployment web --name web-hpa --cpu-percent=70 --min=2 --max=10
kubectl -n hpa-learn get hpa web-hpa

questions.title: HPA v2 on memory
questions.teach:
The `autoscaling/v2` HPA scales on any metric via `spec.metrics`. A **Resource** metric on memory: `{type: Resource, resource: {name: memory, target: {type: Utilization, averageUtilization: 80}}}`.

**Gotcha:** `kubectl autoscale` only does CPU — for memory/custom metrics you write the v2 YAML.
questions.prompt:
In `hpa-learn`, create HPA `api-hpa` (`autoscaling/v2`) for Deployment `api`: scale on **memory** at **80%** average utilization, min **1**, max **6**.

Target: `api-hpa` → api, a Resource/memory metric at 80% Utilization, min 1, max 6.
questions.hint: Write the v2 YAML with `metrics: [{type: Resource, resource: {name: memory, target: {type: Utilization, averageUtilization: 80}}}]`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata: { name: api-hpa, namespace: hpa-learn }
spec:
  scaleTargetRef: { apiVersion: apps/v1, kind: Deployment, name: api }
  minReplicas: 1
  maxReplicas: 6
  metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource: { name: memory, target: { type: Utilization, averageUtilization: 80 } }
YAML

verification.description: api-hpa -> api, memory Utilization 80%, min 1, max 6

questions.title: HPA with multiple metrics
questions.teach:
A v2 HPA can list **several** metrics — it scales to satisfy the one demanding the most replicas. Combine CPU and memory under `spec.metrics`.

**Gotcha:** the HPA takes the **max** desired replicas across all metrics, not the average.
questions.prompt:
In `hpa-learn`, create HPA `cache-hpa` for Deployment `cache` with **two** metrics — CPU at **60%** and memory at **75%** average utilization — min **2**, max **8**.

Target: `cache-hpa` → cache, both CPU(60%) and memory(75%) Resource metrics, min 2, max 8.
questions.hint: Two entries under `metrics:` — one `resource: {name: cpu, ...averageUtilization: 60}` and one `name: memory, ...75`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata: { name: cache-hpa, namespace: hpa-learn }
spec:
  scaleTargetRef: { apiVersion: apps/v1, kind: Deployment, name: cache }
  minReplicas: 2
  maxReplicas: 8
  metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource: { name: cpu, target: { type: Utilization, averageUtilization: 60 } }
  - type: Resource
    resource: { name: memory, target: { type: Utilization, averageUtilization: 75 } }
YAML

verification.description: cache-hpa -> cache, cpu 60% + memory 75%, min 2, max 8

questions.title: Tune scaling behavior
questions.teach:
`spec.behavior` controls how fast the HPA scales. A `scaleDown.stabilizationWindowSeconds` makes it wait before scaling in, to avoid flapping.

**Gotcha:** behavior is split into `scaleUp` and `scaleDown`; the stabilization window smooths the decision over that lookback.
questions.prompt:
In `hpa-learn`, create HPA `worker-hpa` for Deployment `worker`: CPU **50%**, min **1**, max **5**, and a **scaleDown** `stabilizationWindowSeconds` of **300**.

Target: `worker-hpa` → worker, CPU 50%, min 1, max 5, behavior.scaleDown.stabilizationWindowSeconds 300.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata: { name: worker-hpa, namespace: hpa-learn }
spec:
  scaleTargetRef: { apiVersion: apps/v1, kind: Deployment, name: worker }
  minReplicas: 1
  maxReplicas: 5
  metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource: { name: cpu, target: { type: Utilization, averageUtilization: 50 } }
  behavior:
    scaleDown: { stabilizationWindowSeconds: 300 }
YAML

verification.description: worker-hpa: CPU 50%, min 1, max 5, scaleDown stabilization 300

questions.title: Diagnose & fix: HPA shows <unknown>
questions.teach:
An HPA that reports `<unknown>` for CPU can't compute utilization because the target Deployment's container has **no CPU request** — utilization is a percentage *of the request*. Add a request so the HPA has a baseline.

**Gotcha:** HPA percentage metrics are relative to `requests`; without a request there's nothing to divide by.
questions.prompt:
HPA `broke-hpa` in `hpa-learn` targets Deployment `broke` but shows `<unknown>/50%` — it can't scale. Diagnose why and fix the **Deployment** so the HPA can compute CPU utilization. Don't delete the HPA.

Target: Deployment `broke`'s container has a CPU `requests` value set.
questions.hint: `kubectl -n hpa-learn describe hpa broke-hpa` → `<unknown>`. The `broke` Deployment has no CPU request. Add one: `kubectl -n hpa-learn set resources deployment/broke --requests=cpu=100m`.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n hpa-learn set resources deployment/broke --requests=cpu=100m
kubectl -n hpa-learn get deploy broke -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].resources.requests}'

verification.description: Deployment broke now sets a CPU request (HPA can compute)
